You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

What do you mean by “old car makers”—oldest *founded* companies, or makers with the *oldest cars in `cars_data`*?

If you mean “makers with the oldest model years in this database”, here are a few useful queries.

### 1) Oldest year in the dataset per maker
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year_in_data,
  COUNT(*)      AS cars_count
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC, cars_count DESC;
```

### 2) “Old car makers”: makers that have cars at or before a cutoff year
(Example cutoff: 1970)
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  cm.Maker
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
WHERE cd.Year <= 1970
ORDER BY cm.Maker;
```

### 3) Oldest cars (with maker + model) in the dataset
```sql
SELECT
  cd.Year,
  cm.Maker,
  ml.Model,
  cd.MPG,
  cd.Cylinders,
  cd.Horsepower,
  cd.Weight
FROM cars_data cd
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Model  = cn.Model
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id     = ml.Maker
ORDER BY cd.Year ASC, cm.Maker, ml.Model
LIMIT 50;
```

Tell me which definition you want (by founding date vs earliest `Year` in `cars_data`), and if you want a specific cutoff (e.g., “pre-1975”).
focus on makers that produced vehicles a long time ago

```sql
-- Makers that produced vehicles a long time ago (earliest Year in the data)
-- plus how long their span is in the dataset.
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS year_span,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicles_in_data
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING MIN(cd.Year) IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, year_span DESC, vehicles_in_data DESC;
```

If you want “a long time ago” as a cutoff (e.g., makers with any vehicle `Year <= 1970`), tell me the year and I’ll tailor the query.
I want car makers that produced vehicles a long time ago and ensure some were made in 1970.

```sql
-- Makers that have at least one vehicle from 1970,
-- and also produced vehicles earlier than 1970 ("a long time ago")
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS vehicles_1970,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicles_total
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING
  MIN(cd.Year) < 1970
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, vehicles_1970 DESC, vehicles_total DESC;
```
make sure the query also returns the name of each matching car maker

```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker AS car_maker_name,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS earliest_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS latest_year,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS vehicles_1970,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicles_total
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING
  MIN(cd.Year) < 1970
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY earliest_year ASC, car_maker_name;
```
